title: Unit 5: Complete Key Vocabulary & Terminology (25 Words) 📚
content: 📌 Welcome Freshmen Students to Communicative English Skills II (EnLa102) - Unit 5! 👋✨ Here is the complete vocabulary list for Unit 5: Cultural Heritages, formatted In passage-based For Study preparation. ─────────────────────────── 1. Heritage (Noun) • English: Property, traditions, values, or culture passed down through generations. • Amharic: ቅርስ / ውርስ • Synonyms: Inheritance, Legacy, Tradition, Culture • Antonyms: Modernity, Innovation, Novelty • Example: Heritage is anything valued by people today that was also valued by previous generations. ─────────────────────────── 2. Bewilder (Verb) • English: To cause someone to become deeply confused or perplexed. • Amharic: ማደናገር / ግራ ማጋባት • Synonyms: Confuse, Baffle, Perplex, Puzzle • Antonyms: Clarify, Enlighten, Explain, Simplify • Example: Don't let the millions of Google hits to this question bewilder you. ─────────────────────────── 3. Inheritance (Noun) • English: Something that is inherited or passed down from ancestors or previous generations. • Amharic: ውርስ • Synonyms: Bequest, Heritage, Legacy, Endowment • Antonyms: Dispossession, Loss, Forfeiture • Example: Heritage is our inheritance of land, language, ecosystems, knowledge, and culture. ─────────────────────────── 4. Intangible (Adjective) • English: Incapable of being touched or felt physically; non-material beliefs or customs. • Amharic: የማይጨበጥ / ረቂቅ • Synonyms: Abstract, Non-physical, Immaterial, Conceptual • Antonyms: Tangible, Physical, Material, Concrete • Example: Heritage includes intangible beliefs, customs, knowledge, and traditions. ─────────────────────────── 5. Tangible (Adjective) • English: Perceptible by touch; physical or material objects and landmarks. • Amharic: የሚጨበጥ / ቁሳዊ • Synonyms: Physical, Material, Concrete, Touchable • Antonyms: Intangible, Abstract, Immaterial • Example: Tangible heritage consists of physical objects, historical sites, and monuments. ─────────────────────────── 6. Pilgrimage (Noun) • English: A journey to a sacred or religious place for spiritual devotion. • Amharic: የንግሥ / መንፈሳዊ ጉዞ • Synonyms: Religious journey, Expedition, Crusade, Mission • Antonyms: Idle stay, Wandering, Excursion • Example: Examples of cultural heritage include the annual Hajj pilgrimage to Mecca. ─────────────────────────── 7. Unmistakable (Adjective) • English: Impossible to mistake or misunderstand; clear and distinct in signature or style. • Amharic: የማይሳሳት / ግልጽ የሆነ / የታወቀ • Synonyms: Distinct, Clear, Unambiguous, Identifiable • Antonyms: Doubtful, Ambiguous, Unclear, Obscure • Example: Heritage may bear the unmistakable signature of an individual master artist. ─────────────────────────── 8. Vitality (Noun) • English: The state of being strong, active, full of energy, and culturally alive. • Amharic: ሕያውነት / ብርታት / ሕይወት • Synonyms: Liveliness, Vigor, Energy, Animation • Antonyms: Lethargy, Weakness, Inactivity, Lifelessness • Example: Heritage is a fundamental source of individual and group identity, vitality, and solidarity. ─────────────────────────── 9. Solidarity (Noun) • English: Unity or agreement of feeling and action among individuals with common identity. • Amharic: አንድነት / መተባበር / ህብረት • Synonyms: Unity, Harmony, Fellowship, Cohesion • Antonyms: Division, Discord, Disunity, Conflict • Example: Practicing traditional customs builds community identity and social solidarity. ─────────────────────────── 10. Repulsive (Adjective) • English: Arousing intense distaste, disgust, or moral aversion. • Amharic: የሚያስጠላ / የሚያስቆጣ / አስነዋሪ • Synonyms: Disgusting, Offensive, Revolting, Abhorrent • Antonyms: Attractive, Appealing, Pleasing, Charming • Example: Heritage is one of the ways you determine right from wrong and beautiful from repulsive. ─────────────────────────── 11. Descendant (Noun) • English: A person or generation descended from a specific ancestor or ethnic group. • Amharic: ተወላጅ / ዘር / ትውልድ • Synonyms: Offspring, Successor, Heir, Progeny • Antonyms: Ancestor, Forefather, Predecessor • Example: Be mindful of your heritage, for it helps determine your destiny and that of your descendants. ─────────────────────────── 12. Perpetuate (Verb) • English: To make something (a tradition, custom, or meaning) continue indefinitely. • Amharic: እንዲቀጥል ማድረግ / ማቆየት / ማዘለቅ • Synonyms: Maintain, Preserve, Continue, Sustain • Antonyms: Stop, Abolish, Destroy, Discontinue • Example: By definition, heritage only exists and is perpetuated by virtue of the meanings people assign to it. ─────────────────────────── 13. Cherish (Verb) • English: To protect, care for, and hold dear lovingly. • Amharic: በጥብቅ መውደድ / መንከባከብ / ማክበር • Synonyms: Treasure, Value, Protect, Esteem • Antonyms: Despise, Neglect, Disregard, Scorn • Example: Heritage may be cherished and protected at all costs by one group of people. ─────────────────────────── 14. Despise (Verb) • English: To feel deep contempt, strong dislike, or intense hatred for something. • Amharic: መጥላት / መናቅ / ማዋረድ • Synonyms: Hate, Detest, Loathe, Abhor • Antonyms: Cherish, Love, Admire, Respect • Example: Some cultural symbols are cherished by one group while being despised by others. ─────────────────────────── 15. Colossal (Adjective) • English: Extremely large, huge, or massive in physical scale. • Amharic: እጅግ ግዙፍ / ታላቅ • Synonyms: Massive, Enormous, Gigantic, Huge • Antonyms: Tiny, Small, Miniature, Petite • Example: The colossal Buddha statues in Bamiyan Province were destroyed in 2001. ─────────────────────────── 16. Cautionary (Adjective) • English: Serving as a warning or lesson against negative human historical outcomes. • Amharic: ማስጠንቀቂያ አዘል / መማሪያ • Synonyms: Warning, Advisory, Exemplary, Monitory • Antonyms: Encouraging, Complimentary, Favorable • Example: Concentration camps have been preserved as cautionary memorials for humankind. ─────────────────────────── 17. Inalienable (Adjective) • English: Absolute and incapable of being taken away or surrendered. • Amharic: የማይገፈፍ / የማይወሰድ መብት • Synonyms: Absolute, Unchallengeable, Non-transferable, Entrenched • Antonyms: Transferable, Revocable, Changeable • Example: All peoples possess the inalienable right to manage their cultural heritage. ─────────────────────────── 18. Imposition (Noun) • English: The act of enforcing or imposing foreign political, legal, or cultural rules. • Amharic: ጫና / በግድ መጫን / አስገዳጅነት • Synonyms: Enforcement, Burden, Intrusion, Encroachment • Antonyms: Voluntary acceptance, Freedom, Choice • Example: Indigenous peoples have been heavily affected by foreign cultural and economic impositions. ─────────────────────────── 19. Sacrilegious (Adjective) • English: Involving disrespect, violation, or misuse of sacred religious sites or objects. • Amharic: ቅዱስ ነገርን የሚያስነውር / ድፍረት • Synonyms: Blasphemous, Profane, Irreverent, Unholy • Antonyms: Sacred, Reverent, Pious, Holy • Example: Recreational rock climbing on sacred sites is seen as sacrilegious by Native Americans. ─────────────────────────── 20. Imperative (Adjective) • English: Of vital importance; crucial or mandatory for action. • Amharic: እጅግ አስፈላጊ / ግዴታ የሆነ • Synonyms: Crucial, Essential, Vital, Mandatory • Antonyms: Optional, Unimportant, Unnecessary, Voluntary • Example: It is imperative that those engaging with Indigenous heritage do so with care and respect. ─────────────────────────── 21. Prolific (Adjective) • English: Producing much fruit, artwork, literature, or intellectual output. • Amharic: ብዙ የሚያመርት / ፍሬያማ / ምርታማ • Synonyms: Productive, Fruitful, Creative, Fertile • Antonyms: Unproductive, Barren, Unfruitful • Example: The 19th-century artist, whose name I couldn't remember, was very prolific at his time. ─────────────────────────── 22. Deprived (Adjective) • English: Suffering a severe lack of basic material, social, or cultural benefits. • Amharic: የተጎዳ / መሠረታዊ ነገር ያጣ / የተገለለ • Synonyms: Disadvantaged, Underprivileged, Needy, Poor • Antonyms: Privileged, Wealthy, Prosperous • Example: It is usually children from deprived backgrounds that face severe educational problems. ─────────────────────────── 23. Authoritarian (Adjective) • English: Enforcing strict obedience to authority at the expense of personal freedom. • Amharic: አምባገነናዊ / አስገዳጅ • Synonyms: Autocratic, Dictatorial, Domineering, Strict • Antonyms: Democratic, Liberal, Permissive • Example: Children who are born first are often more authoritarian than their younger siblings. ─────────────────────────── 24. Monument (Noun) • English: A statue, building, or structure built to commemorate a notable person or event. • Amharic: ሐውልት / መታሰቢያ • Synonyms: Memorial, Statue, Landmark, Shrine • Antonyms: Ruin, Demolition • Example: Physical heritage includes historic monuments, ancient buildings, and natural sites. ─────────────────────────── 25. Preserve (Verb) • English: To keep intact, protect, and maintain in original condition from loss or damage. • Amharic: መጠበቅ / እንክብካቤ ማድረግ / ጠብቆ ማቆየት • Synonyms: Protect, Safeguard, Maintain, Conserve • Antonyms: Destroy, Neglect, Ruin, Abandon • Example: We have an important responsibility to preserve our cultural heritages for future generations. ─────────────────────────── ❤️ Dear EthioFresh Students!
